clue.text: Graphic publication about section of the Universe

indicators.note: the publication is wrapped about the section, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: a comic is a magazine told in pictures
S is a standard abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: A graphic novel covers some corner of the cosmos.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmic is the adjective describing anything belonging to the universe or outer space.

clue.text: The way up’s hot, by gum?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: the Tao is 'the Way' of Chinese philosophy
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A climb that is hot work, the walker exclaims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By gum!' is a mild northern English exclamation, given as an example with the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild exclamation such as 'by gum' is an example of a swear word or curse.

clue.text: Mediocre individual seizing opening? Loud announcements from me

indicators.note: to seize something is to grab hold of it, so one piece takes another inside it

blocks.note: 'meh' is slang for unimpressive or so-so
a gap is an opening
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: Someone unremarkable takes a chance, then booms out public announcements.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening goes inside the mediocre word straight after its first two letters; the definition is written as if the device itself were speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaphone is the cone that amplifies a voice, so loud messages come out of it.

clue.text: Purpose covering large component of contract

indicators.note: something that covers another wraps around it, holding it inside

blocks.note: a cause is an aim or purpose
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A lawyer's motive hides behind a big part of the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal agreement is made up of numbered sections, each called a clause.

clue.text: Geometrical study extremely dull for MIT – President must intervene

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so this letter is placed inside another word

blocks.note: too means excessively
P is an abbreviation for President
logy is American for sluggish or dull, and MIT is an American university

explanation.surface: A maths subject is deadly boring for the Massachusetts students, so the head must step in.
explanation.walkthrough: MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, signals that the word for dull is American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Topology is the branch of mathematics studying properties of shapes preserved under stretching.

clue.text: Praise for adopting computing technology?

blocks.note: surface reading: a compliment for an organisation that takes up modern computers
setter's reading: computing technology is IT, so the approving phrase is read literally as being fonder of IT

explanation.walkthrough: THAT'S MORE LIKE IT is said when things improve; read literally, it says someone now likes IT more.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an everyday expression of approval when something gets better.

clue.text: A certain hint of carnality during dance, removing a piece of clothing

indicators.note: a hint is only a trace, so just the opening letter of the next word is used
removing means taking something out of the dance's name
during places one thing in the middle of another

blocks.note: one, as in 'one Mr Smith', means a certain person
first letter of carnality
the polka is a lively dance
taken as written, and dropped from the dance

explanation.surface: A dancer, with a touch of sensuality, strips off a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removing a piece of clothing' reads as stripping, but 'a' is the letter dropped from the dance and the definition is just 'piece of clothing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A polo neck is a sweater with a high, folded-over collar, called a turtleneck in America.

clue.text: Measure amount of fertility, getting it up?

indicators.note: an amount of something is only part of it, so the letters are a portion of the next word
in a down entry, raising the letters means reading them from bottom to top

blocks.note: the run of letters inside fertility, before it is turned around

explanation.surface: A sly question about measuring how fertile someone is, with a bawdy hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric unit of volume, so it is a measure.

clue.text: City electors, upset about Unionist, supporting Government

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the voters' letters go round the party member
in a down entry, a piece supporting another sits underneath it

blocks.note: G is an abbreviation for Government
taken as written, to be rearranged
U is an abbreviation for Unionist

explanation.surface: Voters in a city are angry about a Unionist backing the government.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloucester is a cathedral city in the west of England.

clue.text: Son having sex backed devouring dirty mag – disgraceful stuff

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the phrase is read in reverse
dirty suggests something messed up, so its letters are jumbled
devouring means swallowing, so one piece ends up inside the other

blocks.note: S for son, as in genealogies
'at it' is slang for having sex
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A son caught with a porn magazine brings shame on the family.
explanation.walkthrough: AT IT reversed is TITA, which swallows a jumbled MAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Stigmata are marks of shame or disgrace, the plural of stigma.

clue.text: Large amount offered by one working application

blocks.note: a lot is a large amount
I is the Roman numeral one
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A big quantity of something supplied by a person with a job application.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion is a liquid applied to the skin, so it is an application.

clue.text: Condemn to die, with one leaving life

blocks.note: to pass is to die, the one who passes being the one leaving
a life is a prison term of life imprisonment, a kind of sentence

explanation.surface: A judge orders an execution, a single convict going to his death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Condemn to die' looks like the whole definition, but 'to die' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge who passes sentence formally declares the punishment, which is to condemn.

clue.text: Mouthy intervention in roof-top argument turning up in covers of book

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top
a book's covers are its outside, so only the outer letters are used
in places the preceding pieces inside the book's covers

blocks.note: the ridge is the top line of a roof
a row is a quarrel
first and last letters of book

explanation.surface: A noisy row on the roof gets written up in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental bridgework is a fitting a dentist puts in the mouth to replace missing teeth, an oral procedure.

clue.text: Three time runner-up to start with – then I will get Oscar

indicators.note: to start with points to the opening letter only

blocks.note: T is an abbreviation for time
first letter of runner-up
taken as written
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An actor three times second best hopes finally to win an Academy Award.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three people or things.

clue.text: Sports venue not opening? League will withdraw, naturally

indicators.note: without its opening means the first letter is dropped
to withdraw is to pull out, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: a golf course is where golf is played
L is an abbreviation for League

explanation.surface: A sports ground is not opening, so the league pulls out, as you would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: GOLF COURSE loses its first letter G and then its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Of course is an everyday phrase meaning obviously or as expected.

clue.text: Remove University display unit after receiving note

indicators.note: the display unit comes after taking the note on in front of it

blocks.note: uni is short for university
N is an abbreviation for note
a stall is a stand for displaying goods

explanation.surface: A college takes down an exhibition stand after getting a memo.
explanation.definitionFit: To uninstall software is to take it off a computer, so it means to remove.

clue.text: Something wrong on soundtrack curtailed festival for film-maker

indicators.note: a soundtrack is what is heard, so the word is taken by its sound
curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong
Easter is a church festival

explanation.surface: A movie's soundtrack has a fault, and a film festival is cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A cineaste is a devotee of cinema, including someone who makes films.

clue.text: Obsession, namely, holding soccer team back after support ebbs

indicators.note: a tide that ebbs goes back out, so the word runs backwards
back means the team's letters are read in reverse
holding means keeping inside, so the other pieces go within

blocks.note: to feed a family is to support it
a football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals
i.e. means 'that is' or namely

explanation.surface: A fixation, namely, keeping a football team in reserve after fan backing fades.
explanation.definitionFit: An idée fixe is a French phrase for a fixed idea that preoccupies the mind.

clue.text: Indefinable quality linked to the writer repelled couple

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: 'it' is the hard-to-define quality of star appeal
the writer is the setter, who is me

explanation.surface: Some magnetic quality that drives a pair apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like a verb meaning link, but it is the noun for a pair in a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people romantically involved are said to be an item.

clue.text: Wattle and bills indicating avifauna, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letters are used

blocks.note: AC is short for account, a bill, so two of them
first letters of indicating and avifauna

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher reads beaks and wattles as signs of local bird life.
explanation.walkthrough: Wattle is the Australian name for acacia trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacia trees are known in Australia as wattle, so the two are the same plant.

clue.text: American ready to accept Republican that is attending church? They’ll attract attention

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so what follows goes inside
attending means being next to, so one piece sits beside the other

blocks.note: ready means cash, and cents are American money
Rep is short for Republican
i.e. stands for 'that is'
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An American poised to welcome a Republican churchgoer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready is British slang for cash, as in 'the ready'.
explanation.definitionFit: Centrepieces are eye-catching ornaments placed in the middle, so they draw the eye.

clue.text: Ripped, penetrated by hard sharp point

indicators.note: something penetrated has another thing pushed into it

blocks.note: torn means ripped
H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Clothing torn by something stiff and sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is the prickle on a rose stem, a pointed spike.

clue.text: Extremists – in uprooting liberty – will become nasty

indicators.note: extremists suggests the extreme ends, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: first and last letters of uprooting
first and last letters of liberty

explanation.surface: Radicals who tear up freedoms will turn things vicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly can describe a situation that is unpleasant or threatening, as nasty does.

clue.text: Treated poor me, passing water?

indicators.note: something treated is processed and altered, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
us means me in colloquial British speech, as in 'give us a hand'

explanation.surface: A patient laments a urinary problem under medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing water' suggests urinating, but it means letting water through.
explanation.definitionFit: A porous material has tiny holes that let liquid seep through it.

clue.text: Former Chancellor of the Exchequer about to suspend money business

indicators.note: about means around, so the abbreviation goes round the next piece

blocks.note: ex means former
CE is the initials of Chancellor of the Exchequer
to hang something is to suspend it

explanation.surface: An ex-Chancellor is set to halt some financial dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is Britain's finance minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Exchange covers the trading of currencies, as at a bureau de change, a financial business.

clue.text: Least comfortable assessment of allergy?

blocks.note: first meaning: most broke, the superlative of skint, British slang for penniless
second meaning: a test in which allergens are applied to the skin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Comfortable' here means well off; skint is British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as one word it is the poorest; split into two it is a medical patch or prick test.

clue.text: Looking hard to abandon latest European ways

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave behind, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: to be all eyes is to watch intently
E for European; latest says it is the last E that goes

explanation.surface: Staring intently before turning one's back on the newest European fashions.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleys are narrow lanes or passages, kinds of routes or thoroughfares.
